chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from someone else from our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The shroud is slit from the head of the deceased when he is placed in his grave.
ai.seo_question: What is the ritual procedure for handling the shroud when placing the deceased in the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the ritual of slitting the shroud from the head downwards during burial, a practice widely accepted in Shia fiqh to symbolize the soul's ascent or to facilitate the body's direct contact with the earth. Scholars note this act reflects the transition from the worldly covering to the spiritual reality of the grave, emphasizing humility and readiness for the Hereafter.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from someone else from our companions, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Tear (slightly) the shroud from the head of the deceased when you enter his grave’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from more than one person of our people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
a shroud should be cut open from where the head of the deceased is when he is placed in the grave.”
